H4.1 now spells out a three-part noise budget:
- **Rebuild noise:** about ±0.03 pp on the 3-seed mean (E019).
- **Seed noise:** the 3-seed mean SE is about 0.14 pp.
- **RNG-stream re-roll:** the offset of seeds 0–2 from the held-out mean has RMS about 0.23 pp. E016 and E017 are the outliers.

**Status changes:**
- H4.1.1 is narrowed to builds without cudagraphs. H4.3.1 is supported: cudagraph rebuilds are not bit-identical, but the 3-seed mean moves only about 0.03 pp.
- Refuted, because pre-registered results already contradict them: H4.1.3, H2.2.3, H2.5.1 and H1.5.3.
- H4.2.3 is supported: E012's timing shows 9.5 true epochs.
- Moved to inconclusive, because each rests on one 3-seed difference within noise: H1.3.1 (LS), H1.3.4 (LR floor) and H1.5.2 (width).
- Lowered: H1.5.1 to 0.45 (the held-out gain is +0.24 pp and confounded with E015's compile change) and H1.5 to 0.45 (the committee voted refuted 4/4). H1.2.1 lost E006's support because E006 changed optimizer and batch size together.
- H4.2 is restated in true epochs: about 0.44 pp and 0.68 s per epoch, roughly 1.5 s/pp. This is still the cheapest dial. The −0.5 epoch half of H4.2.4 has not been run.

**Counterexamples explained:**
- **E006:** new Lvl1 N1 says step count and batch size are a lever separate from epochs. Batch 2500 and batch 1500 tests are added under it.
- **E016:** filter renormalization may make the filter wd do nothing (H1.5.4 raised to 0.6). H4.1.4 tests whether E016's 0.7607 reproduces from a fresh build.
- **E018:** H2.3 is now supported only for the mild E007 schedule, with three candidate mechanisms. Two tests separate them: H2.3.5 (phase order and the size of the final jump) and H2.3.3, now aimed at BN recalibration on E018.

**Other changes:**
- H2.2's claim that at most 5% systems headroom remains is now marked unmeasured. New Lvl1 N2 proposes that kernel throughput is poor on small feature maps.
- Added from search: BN recalibration on the tip, scored on held-out seeds (H1.3.6, conf 0.35, based on +0.55 pp in arXiv 2411.18704); LS 0.1 and Muon lr ×2; the paired wd ×1 vs ×0.5 test; FreezeOut (H2.6); selective backprop only in mid-training (H2.4.2); and an eval compliance sweep over every B from 1 to 1024 (H3.1.2).
- H1.2.3 lowered to 0.25, since the NS step count may already be 3.

N1 and N2 are the two open Lvl1 hypotheses.

**Recommended next steps:** the −0.5 true-epoch trim, BN recalibration, the E016 re-run, the per-layer profile, and the eval sweep. Score every keep decision on the held-out 10-seed mean."}

On the E018 schedule, recomputing BN stats at 32 px on at most 5k training images after the EMA swap (timed, under 0.1 s) recovers at least 0.3 pp of the held-out mean.

updates.statement: Progressive resizing is a near-linear time dial: step time scales with pixel count (about 0.51/0.71/0.89 s per epoch at 24/28/32 px, E012). Its accuracy cost is mild only for the E007 schedule (24/28/32 at 40/30/30). Every more aggressive variant has an exchange rate of about 0.8–1.0 s/pp, worse than the epoch dial at about 1.5 s/pp: E011 added 20 px and cut the 32 px tail to 20%; E018 dropped 28 px (−0.68 pp held-out). Candidate mechanisms: (a) low resolution during the peak-LR window, where most features are learned; (b) a large final resolution jump that shifts object scale and BN statistics (FixRes); (c) E007's own cost was underestimated because E006 was a lucky 3-seed draw.
updates.reason: Both of its later experiments refute more aggressive schedules (E011-, E018-), so support is limited to the mild schedule. The E018 counterexample is now covered by mechanisms (a), (b) and (c).
The committee voted 3 refuted, 1 unknown. E018 showed that even a single-factor resolution cut costs about 0.8 s/pp, so an early 20 px phase is unlikely to stay within 0.25 pp.
The committee voted refuted 4/4. LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 (E013), which makes a large size-dependent LS effect unlikely. The test is cheap and time-neutral, so it stays open at low priority.

updates.statement: Removing kernel-launch and Python overhead speeds up each step without changing the math. compile plus a fused optimizer gave −14% (E004). After that the step is GPU-bound: CUDA graphs gave −0.9% (E015) and removing graph breaks −0.5% (E017). Whether the conv kernels run at reference airbench throughput (about 112 TFLOP/s) has not been measured.
updates.reason: Review: the claim that at most 5% remains was never measured, and E021's sublinear width scaling hints at poor tensor-core use. The overhead half is measured; the kernel-efficiency half moves to H2.2.4 and the new kernel-efficiency Lvl1.
The committee is split 2–2, so this needs the decisive one-trace profile. Search calibrates the reference at about 112–114 TFLOP/s from airbench's records.

Search: airbench94_muon and Hiverge already use 3 NS iterations, so the port may have no 5→3 headroom. Published cheaper orthogonalizers cap end-to-end savings at about 1–3%, and Muon's total overhead was +3.8% (E006). Reaching ≥1.5% is unlikely.

Review: E006 changed the optimizer and the batch size (1024→2000) together and never ran SGD tuned at batch 2000, so E006 is inconclusive for this prediction (E006~). The new step-count Lvl1 and H1.2.2 separate the two effects.
The committee voted supported 4/4, but the only evidence (E006) is confounded with batch size. Kept open until H1.2.2 runs.

E012's per-epoch timing settles it: 10 loops (4 at 24 px, 1 at 28, 2 full at 32, plus a half loop, ≈9.5 true epochs at a 40/30/30 split). The committee voted supported 4/4. E009 and E010 were built on the E008 base (9.5 true epochs), not on E007, as their times show.

updates.statement: Near the tip, true epochs are a smooth dial: about 0.44 pp of held-out accuracy and about 0.68 s per true epoch (about 1.5 s/pp; E020 vs E017 held-out). The 3-seed slope from E008 (about 0.36 pp per epoch) is consistent with this. It is the cheapest dial measured so far: resizing beyond E007 costs 0.8–1.0 s/pp and the group-2 width about 1.0 s/pp.
updates.reason: Two consistent measurements (E008 3-seed, E020 held-out), now stated in true epochs.
E008: −0.18 pp, −4.8% time, 0.7572 ≥ 0.756. That single diff is within noise, but E020's held-out slope (about 0.22 pp per 0.5 epoch) agrees with it.
The −1.0 point (E020) supports the slope half: 0.44 pp held-out, −10.5% time. The actionable −0.5 point has not been run. The held-out slope predicts about 0.7555 at about 6.2 s.
The committee is split (2 refuted, 2 unknown). Search caps documented gains in short runs at about 10%, and only with full-data phases. A cheaper variant is added as H2.4.2.

new.statement: At a fixed number of data passes, the optimizer step count (batch size) and the optimizer type set accuracy independently of the epoch count. E006 gained +0.66 pp with about half as many steps (batch 1024→2000 together with Muon). Muon's orthogonalized updates appear to have a large critical batch, so step count is a lever that can be traded for time separately from epochs.

Under Muon, the batch size can be moved without the accuracy penalty SGD would pay. Larger batches cut step count and per-step overhead and improve GPU use in the low-resolution phases. Smaller batches add steps, which may buy accuracy that is cheaper than adding epochs.

On the E017 tip at the same true epoch count, raising batch from 2000 to 2500 (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, schedules stretched to the new step count) keeps the held-out seeds 3–12 mean within 0.15 pp of 0.7577 and cuts mean time by at least 1.5%.

On the E017 tip at the same true epoch count, lowering batch from 2000 to 1500 (same scaling rules) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.25 pp at no more than +3% time. That rate would beat the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp).

The GPU-bound step still runs below reference airbench throughput on the small feature maps (7×7 and 3×3 at 24–28 px; group 3). A systems lever worth at least 5% therefore remains at identical math, through channel padding, cuDNN algorithm choice, or a different batch layout in the low-resolution phases.
Tensor-core use drops on small spatial maps: E021 cut group-2 MACs 15.5% but time only 7.8%. So the per-pixel cost at low resolution and in the late groups is higher than at 32 px in group 1.

A per-layer torch.profiler trace of one E017 step at each resolution shows the layer-weighted achieved throughput at 24 px at least 20% below that at 32 px. It also shows group 3 below 70 TFLOP/s at every resolution.

Re-running E016 (commit d360673) through ar.py from a fresh build reproduces its seeds 0–2 mean within 0.05 pp of 0.7607. That would make E016's +0.43 pp offset from the held-out mean a persistent seed×RNG-stream effect rather than a build or harness artifact.
On the E017 tip (wd ×0.5), lowering label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.1 (near Hiverge's 0.09) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp at unchanged time.

On the E017 tip, doubling the Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.48, with everything else unchanged, raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp. This follows E014's slightly upward trend, now on the lower-wd base.
Paired single-factor test on one build lineage: on the E017 tip, restoring wd ×1 (from ×0.5) lowers the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp compared with 0.7577.

The size of the final resolution jump, not the 28 px features themselves, drives E018's loss. Swapping the order of the first two phases to 28→24→32 (40/30/30 of steps at 28/24/32 px, so the 28 px phase still runs at peak LR) keeps time and pixel cost close to E017 but has a 24→32 jump like E018. This schedule loses at least 0.3 pp of the held-out mean vs E017.

FreezeOut-style truncation of the backward pass: late in training, the whitening layer and group 1, which run at the highest resolution, change little. Stopping gradients into them cuts their weight-gradient and input-gradient FLOPs and keeps their capacity.

On the E017 tip, stopping backprop into the whitening layer and group 1 for the last 25% of steps, with their LR annealed to 0 by that point, cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.2 pp of the held-out seeds 3–12 mean.

On the E017 tip, selective backprop applied only between 50% and 90% of steps (select on a 0.5× resolution forward pass, backprop the top 50% by loss, every other batch) cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.2 pp of the held-out mean.

On the E017 tip (max-autotune+cudagraphs, error_on_recompile on after build), an eval sweep over every B in 1..1024 returns finite [B, 100] logits, each call under 5 s, with no recompile error. If this fails, eval is going through a shape-specialized compiled path and every result since E008 or E015 is at compliance risk.

structured_output.summary:
I made the noise model and bookkeeping match the loop's own data. H4.1 now spells out a three-part noise budget:
- **Rebuild noise:** about ±0.03 pp on the 3-seed mean (E019).
- **Seed noise:** the 3-seed mean SE is about 0.14 pp.
- **RNG-stream re-roll:** the offset of seeds 0–2 from the held-out mean has RMS about 0.23 pp. E016 and E017 are the outliers.

**Status changes:**
- H4.1.1 is narrowed to builds without cudagraphs. H4.3.1 is supported: cudagraph rebuilds are not bit-identical, but the 3-seed mean moves only about 0.03 pp.
- Refuted, because pre-registered results already contradict them: H4.1.3, H2.2.3, H2.5.1 and H1.5.3.
- H4.2.3 is supported: E012's timing shows 9.5 true epochs.
- Moved to inconclusive, because each rests on one 3-seed difference within noise: H1.3.1 (LS), H1.3.4 (LR floor) and H1.5.2 (width).
- Lowered: H1.5.1 to 0.45 (the held-out gain is +0.24 pp and confounded with E015's compile change) and H1.5 to 0.45 (the committee voted refuted 4/4). H1.2.1 lost E006's support because E006 changed optimizer and batch size together.
- H4.2 is restated in true epochs: about 0.44 pp and 0.68 s per epoch, roughly 1.5 s/pp. This is still the cheapest dial. The −0.5 epoch half of H4.2.4 has not been run.

**Counterexamples explained:**
- **E006:** new Lvl1 N1 says step count and batch size are a lever separate from epochs. Batch 2500 and batch 1500 tests are added under it.
- **E016:** filter renormalization may make the filter wd do nothing (H1.5.4 raised to 0.6). H4.1.4 tests whether E016's 0.7607 reproduces from a fresh build.
- **E018:** H2.3 is now supported only for the mild E007 schedule, with three candidate mechanisms. Two tests separate them: H2.3.5 (phase order and the size of the final jump) and H2.3.3, now aimed at BN recalibration on E018.

**Other changes:**
- H2.2's claim that at most 5% systems headroom remains is now marked unmeasured. New Lvl1 N2 proposes that kernel throughput is poor on small feature maps.
- Added from search: BN recalibration on the tip, scored on held-out seeds (H1.3.6, conf 0.35, based on +0.55 pp in arXiv 2411.18704); LS 0.1 and Muon lr ×2; the paired wd ×1 vs ×0.5 test; FreezeOut (H2.6); selective backprop only in mid-training (H2.4.2); and an eval compliance sweep over every B from 1 to 1024 (H3.1.2).
- H1.2.3 lowered to 0.25, since the NS step count may already be 3.

N1 and N2 are the two open Lvl1 hypotheses.

**Recommended next steps:** the −0.5 true-epoch trim, BN recalibration, the E016 re-run, the per-layer profile, and the eval sweep. Score every keep decision on the held-out 10-seed mean.
